content:
Amanda: quick sync — idea: collapse several model namespaces (prod-v1, prod-v2, canary, staging) into a single epoched namespace (epoch_id=2026-03) + alias layers so routing + rollouts are simpler.

Kevin: sounds promising. what's the migration story?

Amanda: plan sketch: 1) introduce epoch manifest, 2) populate aliases pointing to existing pins, 3) soft-read route clients to epoch namespace, 4) GC old labels after grace.

Raj: main risks i see: client SDKs that expect flat model ids, and clients doing string-equality for pins. we need a compat shim.

Sasha: agree. Also telemetry: we must emit both "legacy_model" and "epoch_ref" on the first month so downstream billing/alerts don't break.

Amanda: good call. telemetry fields proposal: epoch_ref, alias_chain, origin_stamp, soft_ttl, hard_ttl. we can hook these into console and rollouts UI.

Kevin: what about rollback? if we collapse namespaces and something goes wrong, can we atomically switch back?

Amanda: we'd keep stable alias backlinks. rollback = re-point alias to previous epoch manifest. will require atomic write with manifest fingerprint.

Raj: suggest adding a provenance field so we can detect manifests created from migration vs user-created. i.e. provenance: "migration-2026-03-10".

Sasha: operational GC rules? soft_ttl vs hard_ttl semantics please.

Amanda: proposal: soft_ttl = advisory eviction (clients can be probed); hard_ttl = absolute GC window. During migration we set long soft_ttl (30d) and long hard_ttl (90d) so we can revert easily.

Amanda: sample manifest snippet:
{
  "epoch_id": "2026-03",
  "namespace": "prod",
  "model": "redwood/gpt-13b.v2",
  "aliases": ["gpt-13b-stable", "gpt-13b-merchant"],
  "provenance": "migration-2026-03-10",
  "soft_ttl": "30d",
  "hard_ttl": "90d",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:abcd..."
}

Kevin: nice. one more: client resolution order. i propose: 1) explicit client pin (if present) 2) alias lookup 3) epoch-latest fallback 4) configured global fallback. That keeps explicit pins honored.

Elaine: ops note: we need a rollout plan that throttles alias rebind rate to avoid thundering across shared caches. e.g., 100 binds/min per region.

Raj: also think about cross-tenant edgecases — tenants with hard locks should be exempt from automatic alias migration. add tenant_overrides in manifest.

Amanda: yes. manifest schema extension: "tenant_overrides": ["tenant-id-foo"].

Sasha: how do we represent partial rollouts (cohorts)? we already have cohorts for canary; can epoch manifest include a cohort map?

Amanda: include an optional cohorts mapping: {"cohortA": {"percent": 10, "alias": "gpt-13b-cohortA"}}. the routing layer will interpret it.

Kevin: testing plan? we need an integration test that validates: alias binding, alias rollback, telemetry emitted, GC respects hard_ttl.

Amanda: i'll draft a follow-up RFC with schema, migration playbook, and test checklist. will post link here when ready.

Deploy-bot: RFC document created: https://docs.internal/rfcs/epoch-namespace-consolidation (draft) :party_parrot:

Sasha: tiny nit — name field: use "epoch_id" rather than plain epoch to avoid collisions with other metadata.

Amanda: noted. will use epoch_id in draft.

Kevin: 👍 once RFC is up i'll run a quick design review session.

Raj: thanks everyone — i can help with client shim PRs.

Amanda: thanks all, will follow up with RFC + migration timeline.
